* **Limitations:** Requires efficient culling and bounding box calculation to avoid processing non-intersecting primitives, and performance may degrade with high primitive density and overlap [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly supports all components of the claim. 1. 'Requires efficient culling and bounding box calculation': The text describes transforming primitives by the projection matrix to process only those visible (culling) and calculating a 'valid depth range' based on the support radius and covariance (bounding box calculation) to determine which ray segments to update. 2. 'Avoid processing non-intersecting primitives': The algorithm iterates only over the calculated depth range (index_start to index_end), effectively skipping non-intersecting segments. 3. 'Performance may degrade with high primitive density and overlap': The text states that the naive approach (which the optimized method addresses) incurs 'significant overhead' and that the problem 'comes particularly problematic in regions with overlapping primitives,' implying that without these specific optimizations (or in general high-density scenarios), performance is a concern.

Per-primitive ray sampling is a rendering strategy where each geometric primitive (specifically ellipsoids) independently updates only the ray segments it intersects, avoiding redundant parameter loads and enabling accurate Transfer Function (TF) mapping by accumulating contributions in 3D space [S1, unofficial].

The claim accurately reflects the content of Source [S1]. The source explicitly describes a 'per-primitive ray sampling strategy' where 'each ellipsoid independently updates only the ray segments it intersects.' It confirms that this approach avoids 'redundant parameter loads' (by processing each primitive once and caching parameters) and enables accurate Transfer Function (TF) mapping by 'accumulating contributions in 3D space' (specifically, accumulating intensity in ray segments which represent 3D positions along the ray). All specific details mentioned in the claim are present in the provided text.
